title: A backward org makes the linker hand out wrong label addresses, with nothing to notice it.
detail: Last-match scan over a table a backward org makes non-monotonic. Reproduced by derivation from the existing org_backward_overwrite test with a growing stub: correct 7, returns 5. Parcel out on branch parcel/shift-offset-org. Seats P2 and CACHE hit the same function for COST, not for this defect; that pair is recorded separately.

title: A bit test against a PC-relative label writes its address over the bit number, emitting a valid instruction that means something else.
detail: Both front-ends pass a hardcoded extension offset of 2; encode_bit emits the bit-number word first, so the correct offset is 4 (static) and 5 (indexed). The repo's own capstone_diff support module documents the asl witness 083A 0001 0002. Byte-neutral: aeon has no btst pcrel site. Parcel out on branch parcel/btst-pcrel-offset.

title: One language's align still writes padding bytes the other language stopped writing two days ago, and the test comparing them cannot see the difference.
detail: AS moved to reserve + asl_align_pad at 84c48a7b and touched only that side; .emp still emits Fill and rounds up unsigned where the shared rule is signed. The parity gate places data after the align in all three cases and flattens with 0x00, so fill and no-fill are identical. MUST land with the DAC bank recompute or the drum bank moves off its boundary silently.

title: The address-of-here builtin is baked before placement while labels follow placement, so the two disagree.
detail: The comment justifying same-section-only tracking says staleness hits labels and here() equally; that stopped being true at the placement rework. No here() test runs a placement pass. Exposure is data sections, not code, because a relaxable branch makes here() provisional and therefore correct.

title: A source file missing one closing keyword quietly loses a byte and reports success.
detail: find_block_end treats the file's last line as the missing closer. Reproduced against a real binary: AA 01 02 03 04 where AA 01 02 03 04 05 is correct, exit 0. Twelve lines away the code refuses a no-verdict if condition for precisely this reason. This is the class the AS-replacement project exists to eliminate.

title: A macro that calls itself twice never finishes, because only its depth is capped.
detail: Depth cap 64, breadth unbounded. The same file already argues the global-budget case for nested while and adds one; it was never carried to macros. Reached in practice via the unterminated-block defect, which can manufacture a recursive macro from source that never contained one.

title: A repeat block has no iteration limit at all, so a large count hangs the assembler with no diagnostic.
detail: while checks two caps; rept checks neither. Nested empty repeats reach ten billion body runs and time out silently.

title: One stray byte in a RAM-placed section makes the linker try to allocate the whole address space and die without a diagnostic.
detail: flatten sizes its output buffer from a placed ADDRESS rather than a size. Allocation failure aborts, so catch_unwind cannot turn it into an error. The correct guard, validate_section, exists and is not on the CLI path.

title: Two data directives silently truncate an out-of-range value where the third refuses it.
detail: dc.b range-checks and errors; dc.w and dc.l cast. The comment eight lines below the truncating line argues at length that truncating is the silent-wrong-bytes class.

title: Seven separate reviewers found the same mistake: something is checked in one place and then used somewhere that never sees the check.
detail: Sites: AS align (i64 guard, u32 consumer, panics in release); ds.b/w/l; .emp bank attribute; Z80 symbolic addresses on a truncating fixup where the emp twin range-checks; dc.w/dc.l; the abs.w window checked on three paths and not the eager fourth; comptime checked arithmetic against link-time wrapping. The correct idiom is already present at three sites, so these are drifts. Ruled to land as ONE parcel.

title: The lint guaranteeing every skipped check announces itself is blind to a wrapped line, and five live announcements are already through the hole.
detail: It only reads a format literal beginning on the same line as the macro. The five live sites say NOT MEASURED, which is in its own forbidden vocabulary, and are green only because of a line break. There is no rustfmt config and no fmt check, and five compliant sites already exceed the default width, so a routine reformat would shrink the census.

title: Four documents say the landing bar fails on a skipped check; the landing bar never reads the skip count.
detail: The exit decision reads CARGO_RC, FAILED, CLIPPY_RC and RECONCILED. The only real enforcer is the nightly lane, which is not the landing bar. A strict landing run carrying skip lines prints RESULT GREEN and exits 0.

title: The guard certifying that a byte-moving freeze was proved on an emulator only checks that the field is not empty.
detail: Five anchor-moving freezes satisfy it with an ab value that is the name of the preceding chain entry, chaining back to the bare string master.

title: Three port tests carry comments claiming a proof the code does not perform.
detail: The zero is the branch condition, not an assertion; one arm asserts a slice is empty when its own bounds make it empty by construction. A prior sweep hardened the comparison helper and missed the arm that skips the helper, so the hardened helper now makes the trio look covered.

title: A generated field the manifest calls dead is still stamped into hundreds of lines, and names test binaries that do not exist.
detail: repin.toml declares the tests field no longer read by anything while repin.rs still renders it. Three named binaries are absent from the tree, on the two most-read constants in pins.rs.

title: A number of pinned regions have no consumer anywhere in the code.
detail: ADJUDICATED: seat GATE reported 33 with an unstated predicate; seat B2b enumerated 22 with line numbers, a stated predicate and a control. The packet takes the enumerated set, on this lane's own rule to write the set and never the count. Spot-checked two plus the control.

title: The project's continuous integration has been failing for ten days, and the failing check is the one guaranteeing a bare run refuses.
detail: Last green 2026-08-27T11:18:17Z. The failing rows are bare_run_refuses.rs, and CI is the declared partial run whose refusal they exist to observe. Found on the hub's ask after oracle measured theirs.

title: A sigil test compiles a live file from another repo, so its subject moves under it and reddens this lane's nightly gate on a defect that does not exist.
detail: Diagnosed by the aeon lane from the source-gate red and verified here. Ruled: a small sigil-owned fixture, never a widened ambient, because widening breaks the next time anyone touches a live game file. Fixture named to aeon; they carve it. Implies a sweep of every read_aeon site naming a game file rather than an engine vocabulary file.

title: Sound-head addresses in seven test files still name the bank they lived in before the re-layout, in the doc comments and the failure messages.
detail: The assertions derive their values and are correct; only the prose is stale. When one of these gates goes red it tells the reader to look a long way from where the bytes are. Verified against the frozen size table.

title: A block body is re-read once for every level of nesting it sits inside, which the reference assembler does not do at all.
detail: Flat in asl, linear here: at depth 32 it is roughly fifty times slower. Near-invisible on the corpus this project benchmarks with (mean nesting depth 0.054) and dominant on the engine (1.157) and on the Sonic 2 disassembly. MEASURE-FIRST: size it on aeon or s2disasm, never on s1disasm.

title: The assembler reads the whole source one more time than the reference does, to prove to itself that nothing changed.
detail: Convergence requires two consecutive identical symbol tables, so the floor is two traversals where asl stops at one, plus one more per forward-referenced equate link. Reached by two seats using different instruments: a pass census forward, marginal-pass calibration in reverse.

title: Rendering one diagnostic walks the source file from the beginning, so an error near the end of a large file is expensive.
detail: Cost depends on both file size and error position, which is what walking from byte zero looks like. Invisible on a corpus with few diagnostics and heavy on one with thousands, and it only bites a FAILING build, which is the build a developer repeats.

title: A masking rule is written out twice in one crate with no shared constant, and the second copy is unreachable.
detail: Its guard flag is constructed nowhere in the repository, verified against a control. The sibling builtin shares a named constant between its two sites; this one does not. If the window ever moves, the live copy is fixed and the dead one is resurrected wrong.

title: A finding deferred in August now costs more than the number everyone is quoting.
detail: Re-derived rather than quoted: the count moved from 53 to 59, six new procs, all engine code written since. The model was validated by reproducing the historical 53 at three separate sweep-era revisions, which is the control that makes the new number credible. The in-code doc and the ledger both state the stale one.

title: The crate split deferred in August is now about seventy percent larger than when it was deferred.
detail: The harness doubled in size and gained a dependency the seam plan predates. Its build-timing half is unmeasurable without a build and those seconds should not be quoted as current.

title: A reviewer's pinned instrument was deleted mid-measurement by another agent sharing the same scratch directory.
detail: Two agents told to write scratch files and not told where are each other's concurrent writer by construction. Every future seat brief names a private scratch directory. The affected seat re-copied, re-verified its digest and re-ran, and retracted the one contaminated number.

title: The Z80 instruction encoder was checked against the reference assembler across hundreds of forms and emits no wrong bytes.
detail: The heaviest measurement in the panel: an independent model transcribed from the encoder, validated against 150 reference-minted vectors, its own harness mutation-checked, then 863 forms swept one reference invocation each with exit status checked. Specifically refuted: no prefixed instruction family silently falls back to its unprefixed form. Recorded as a clean result so a quiet area is not read as an unexamined one.

title: Two reviewers disagreed about whether a linker function is slow, and both were right about different inputs.
detail: ADJUDICATED: P2 measured the AS path, where the whole program is a handful of huge sections and the cost is real; CACHE measured the .emp path, where each module gets its own sections and it is negligible. Neither said which corpus it measured. On the AS path the same function is both quadratic and wrong for one underlying reason, and org exists only there, so one fix addresses both.

title: The Z80 instruction encoder was checked against the reference assembler across hundreds of forms and emits no wrong bytes.
detail: State corrected from decided to holds, the state added to the contract on this row's own first use. The finding is unchanged: an independent model validated against reference-minted vectors, its own harness mutation-checked, then hundreds of forms swept one reference invocation each with exit status checked, and no wrong bytes. Recorded so a quiet area is not read as an unexamined one.

title: Two reviewers disagreed about whether a linker function is slow, and both were right about different inputs.
detail: State corrected from decided to OPEN, NOT to holds. The contract pairs holds with severity clean, a property re-derived and found to hold; this row is severity low and nothing here holds. What was settled is the DISAGREEMENT (two seats measured different corpora and neither said so); the cost itself is real, unfixed, and lives on the AS path where the whole program is a handful of large sections. It is expected to close as a side effect of the correctness parcel now out, since one fix addresses both, and it gets its own fixed line if it does.
